references.text: God forbade making gods of gold or silver, which the people broke by making the golden calf
Describes the actual event where Aaron made the golden calf that Moses refers to in his prayer
Moses' earlier intercession for the people after the same sin with the golden calf
Moses recounts how he fell down before the Lord because of the people's great sin with the golden calf
Moses' intercession for the people after the golden calf incident, parallel to his prayer in Exodus 32
Jeroboam repeats the sin of making golden calves and calls them the gods of Israel
The psalm describes how Israel made a calf at Horeb and forgot God who saved them
Stephen refers to the golden calf incident in his speech, where the people made a calf and sacrificed to the idol
Jesus Christ as advocate with the Father reminds us of Moses' role as intercessor for the people's sins
Direct narrative connection: 32:21 is Moses' confrontation with Aaron about the sin that 32:31 confesses before God.
Theological parallel: The pattern of the people sinning, confessing, and Moses taking on the role of intercessor.
Contrastive parallel: Pharaoh confesses for his own deliverance, while Moses confesses for the people.
Direct narrative connection: God's observation that the people are stiff-necked (v.9) is confirmed by Moses in his prayer (v.31).
Direct narrative connection: God's accusation that the people have acted corruptly (v.7) is confirmed by Moses (v.31).
